findings.claim: unsubscribe returns a 500 (NoMethodError on nil) when the logged-in user has no TopicUser row for the topic, because TopicUser.find_by can return nil and line 107 calls tu.notification_level without a check.
findings.evidence: Lines 105-107 have no nil guard. OCR cites PostAlerter using TopicUser.get(...).try(:notification_level) (post_alerter.rb:22,105) as proof the row can be missing for @mentioned users. Superpowers says mailed recipients get a row via TopicUser.change, but forwarded, shared or hand-typed links still crash. Proposed controller spec: log in, GET :unsubscribe on a fresh topic, expect success. Expected failure is NoMethodError. Not executed.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats (ponytail flagged it outside its lane without assessing it). The seats disagree on whether mail recipients always have a row, but the crash path stands either way. Make it red first with the proposed spec in spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb.

findings.claim: The unsubscribe endpoint changes notification state on a plain GET with no CSRF protection and no signed per-user token. A third-party page (for example an img tag) or a link prefetcher can change a logged-in user's notification level for any topic they can see.
findings.evidence: Routes at 440-441 are plain get. The action calls tu.save! (topics_controller.rb:98-115). Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and check_xhr is skipped (line 32). The digest unsubscribe uses a per-user key (routes.rb:202). All seats marked this as reasoned only.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats (ponytail's prefetcher point is the same GET-safety defect). The red test is a request spec showing that a cross-origin-style GET with no token mutates notification_level. It must fail on the pinned code before the fix.

findings.claim: The action steps the level down one notch instead of setting a target level, so it is not idempotent. A reload, second click or history replay moves watching to regular and then to muted, which the user never chose.
findings.evidence: Lines 107-111: a level above regular becomes regular, anything else becomes muted. All seats marked this as reasoned only.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats. Red test: GET :unsubscribe twice for a watching user and expect the level not to be muted. This fails on the pinned code.

findings.claim: The confirmation copy says 'You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}', but a first click from watching or tracking only drops the level to regular. At regular the user is still notified (and emailed) for replies, mentions and quotes, so the feature does not do what the page and email promise.
findings.evidence: Server mapping at topics_controller.rb:107-111. The message is rendered via controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-7. OCR rated this Minor; mattpocock and superpowers rated it Important as part of a larger point. Normalised to Important as a spec-level mismatch with the PR title.
findings.reason: Raised by 3 seats. Red test: a watching user hits unsubscribe and the spec asserts they no longer receive reply notifications, or that the copy matches the resulting level. Settle the intended target level when fixing.

findings.claim: A logged-out recipient who clicks the email link is redirected to / by the NotLoggedIn handler. Nothing is unsubscribed, no message is shown, and there is no return path to the unsubscribe page.
findings.evidence: :unsubscribe sits behind ensure_logged_in (mattpocock cites line 27, OCR line 28). application_controller.rb:97-104 calls redirect_to path('/') for non-JSON GET without saving a destination. Reasoned only. Mattpocock rated it Minor, OCR Important.
findings.reason: Raised by 3 seats (ponytail out of lane, unassessed). Normalised to the correctness seat's Important because the feature silently fails for its main audience. Red test: a logged-out GET :unsubscribe should end on a login flow that returns to the unsubscribe URL; it currently redirects to /.

findings.claim: An in-app Ember transition to the topicUnsubscribe route only loads topic JSON and never calls the server action, yet still shows the 'You will stop receiving notifications' confirmation.

findings.reason: Raised by 3 seats (ponytail out of lane, unassessed). Minor, so no red test is required, but an acceptance test for an in-app transition would guard it.

findings.claim: tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change. No MessageBus notification_level_change is published, so other tabs go stale. notifications_reason_id is not set to user_changed and notifications_changed_at is not stamped.
findings.evidence: TopicUser.change (topic_user.rb:77-115) does all three. The existing set_notifications action (topics_controller.rb:330-334) uses it. The client route nulls details.notificationReasonText (routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:14) to hide the stale reason.
findings.reason: Raised by 2 seats, so appendix and not fixed this pass. ponytail: switching to TopicUser.change likely also resolves the nil-row crash.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored: no build, test, lint or type check results exist, and every finding is reasoned. All proposed red tests are unexecuted. No spec was given; all seats used the PR title 'FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails' as the implicit spec. Standards axis: only CONTRIBUTING.md ('Code', 'Coding Conventions') exists; there are no other standards docs. Files: all four seats report reviewing all 18 files. OCR's tool excluded 7 files (six .js.es6 as unsupported_ext, plus spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb as default_path), and the seat reviewed them manually. Mattpocock only lightly reviewed app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss and app/assets/javascripts/discourse/views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6. Superpowers checked app/models/topic_user.rb, app/views/email/notification.html.erb, topic.scss and the view only for behaviour change. Not done by any seat: running tests, rendering the Ember/Handlebars templates, comparing non-English locale files beyond noting the gap. Ponytail did not verify unbound i18n helper update behaviour. No reviewer from a different model family was available. Agreement counts include ponytail's out-of-lane, unassessed flags (nil TopicUser, GET/toggle, in-app transition, logged-out redirect, missing specs); without them, the logged-out redirect and in-app transition findings would drop to the appendix. The single-seat canonical-URL regression (superpowers, Important) sits in the appendix under the agreement rule and is not fixed.
